SimulatedNetwork.cs: using System;
using System.Collections.Generic;
// Name labels the trace. Address is this computer's IP. Gateway is its router interface.
sealed record Host(string Name, string Address, string Gateway)
// This host's route table tells IPv4 where to send a packet next.
// The "default" entry sends packets to Gateway when there is no exact route.
public IReadOnlyDictionary<string, string> Routes { get; } =
new Dictionary<string, string> { ["default"] = Gateway };
// This class models the two kernels' socket tables and the route through one router.
// client and server are the two computers in the example. This one object stores
// both kernels' tables. The local IP in each socket address keeps their entries separate.
sealed class SimulatedNetwork(Host client, Host server)
// A HashSet stores unique entries. Each entry is a local IP and port, such as
// 198.51.100.20:8080. Bind and automatic port assignment add entries here.
// readonly keeps the collection reference fixed. Its contents can still change.
private readonly HashSet<SocketAddress> boundPorts = new();
// Key = the listening IP and port. Value = a queue of completed connections
// waiting for Accept(). Listen creates the queue. The handshake fills it.
private readonly Dictionary<SocketAddress, Queue<Tcp>> listeners = new();
// Key = a pair of IP-and-port addresses. Value = the TCP state for that endpoint.
// The client entry uses (client, server). The server entry uses (server, client).
// Both ends can have different sequence numbers and different receive buffers.
private readonly Dictionary<(SocketAddress Local, SocketAddress Remote), Tcp> connections = new();
// Key = a computer's IP. Value = its Host object, including its default route.
// DeliverSegment uses this to turn the connection's IP addresses into Host objects.
private readonly Dictionary<string, Host> hosts = new()
[client.Address] = client,
[server.Address] = server
// Key = the packet's destination IP. Value = the next-hop IP the router chooses.
// The router can reach both hosts directly, so these entries point to the hosts themselves.
private readonly Dictionary<string, string> routerRoutes = new()
[client.Address] = client.Address,
[server.Address] = server.Address
// Socket.Bind calls this to claim an IP and port before the server starts listening.
public SocketAddress ReservePort(Host host, int port)
if (port is < 1 or > 65535)
throw new ArgumentOutOfRangeException(nameof(port));
var address = new SocketAddress(host.Address, port);
if (!boundPorts.Add(address))
throw new InvalidOperationException($"Port already bound at {address}.");
return address;
// Socket.Listen registers the server address with an empty queue for future connections.
public void StartListening(SocketAddress address) =>
listeners.Add(address, new Queue<Tcp>());
// Socket.Connect calls this. localAddress may be null when the app has skipped Bind.
public Tcp OpenTcpConnection(Host host, SocketAddress? localAddress, SocketAddress remoteAddress)
if (remoteAddress.Ip == host.Address || !hosts.ContainsKey(remoteAddress.Ip))
throw new InvalidOperationException("Connect to the other host in this simulation.");
// Use the bound address if there is one. Otherwise, pick a free client port.
SocketAddress local = localAddress ?? AssignClientPort(host);
// Fixed initial sequence numbers make the example easy to follow.
var tcp = new Tcp(host.Name, local, remoteAddress, 1000, TcpState.Closed);
// Register the client endpoint before sending SYN so the returning SYN+ACK can find it.
connections.Add((local, remoteAddress), tcp);
try
DeliverSegment(tcp, tcp.StartHandshake());
return tcp;
catch
// Release the client state if the simulated connection could not open.
connections.Remove((local, remoteAddress));
if (localAddress is null)
boundPorts.Remove(local);
throw;
// Socket.Accept takes the oldest completed connection from the listening socket's queue.
// The socket layer wraps the returned TCP endpoint in a new connected socket.
public Tcp TakeAcceptedConnection(SocketAddress local)
if (!listeners[local].TryDequeue(out Tcp? tcp))
throw new InvalidOperationException("In this demo, call Accept after the client connects.");
return tcp;
// Scan from port 51000 and reserve the first free port on this host.
private SocketAddress AssignClientPort(Host host)
// Connecting an unbound client socket lets its kernel pick a free port.
for (int port = 51000; port <= 65535; port++)
var address = new SocketAddress(host.Address, port);
if (boundPorts.Add(address))
Console.WriteLine($"[{host.Name} kernel] Assigned local port {port}");
return address;
throw new InvalidOperationException("No simulated client ports are available.");
// Carry a handshake, data, or acknowledgment segment through IPv4 and the router.
public void DeliverSegment(Tcp tcp, TcpSegment segment)
Host sender = hosts[tcp.Local.Ip];
Host receiver = hosts[tcp.Remote.Ip];
TcpSegment? next = segment;
// A SYN+ACK or ACK generated by the receiver travels back through the same IP code.
while (next is not null)
// 1. The sending host looks up a route. Its next hop is the router's local interface.
string gateway = Ipv4.LookupRoute(sender.Name, sender.Routes, receiver.Address);
if (gateway != client.Gateway && gateway != server.Gateway)
throw new InvalidOperationException("The simulated router is unreachable.");
// 2. Wrap the TCP segment in an IPv4 packet. The destination IP is still the final host.
Ipv4Packet packet = Ipv4.CreatePacket(sender, receiver.Address, next);
// 3. The router chooses the next hop and reduces TTL by one as it forwards the packet.
string nextHop = Ipv4.LookupRoute("Router", routerRoutes, packet.Destination);
packet = Ipv4.Forward(packet);
if (nextHop != receiver.Address)
throw new InvalidOperationException("The router chose the wrong next hop.");
// 4. The receiving host unwraps IPv4 and uses the segment's ports to find TCP state.
TcpSegment incoming = Ipv4.UnwrapPacket(receiver, packet);
next = DeliverToTcpConnection(receiver, packet.Source, incoming);
// 5. Swap directions so any reply goes back to the original sender.
(sender, receiver) = (receiver, sender);
// Find the receiving TCP endpoint and hand it the segment. A null result means no reply.
private TcpSegment? DeliverToTcpConnection(Host receiver, string sourceIp, TcpSegment segment)
// The kernel uses both IP addresses and both ports to find the right TCP connection.
var local = new SocketAddress(receiver.Address, segment.DestinationPort);
var remote = new SocketAddress(sourceIp, segment.SourcePort);
// An existing connection handles this segment. A first SYN can open a new one below.
if (!connections.TryGetValue((local, remote), out Tcp? tcp))
if (segment.Flags != TcpFlags.Syn || !listeners.ContainsKey(local))
throw new InvalidOperationException($"No TCP connection or listening port at {local}.");
Console.WriteLine($"[{receiver.Name} kernel] SYN matched listening socket at {local}");
// This is the server's TCP state for one client. Accept returns its app socket later.
tcp = new Tcp(receiver.Name, local, remote, 5000, TcpState.Listen);
connections.Add((local, remote), tcp);
TcpState previousState = tcp.State;
TcpSegment? reply = tcp.ReceiveSegmentFromIpv4(segment);
// The final ACK completes the server's handshake. Queue the connection for Accept.
if (previousState == TcpState.SynReceived && tcp.State == TcpState.Established)
listeners[local].Enqueue(tcp);
Console.WriteLine($"[{receiver.Name} kernel] Handshake complete. Queue connection for Accept().");
return reply;
